newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lankans begin voting to elect local councils.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lankans begin voting to elect local councils.

text.p: Sri Lankans began voting on Friday to elect members to 238 local councils in what is widely seen to be the first political test for President Chandrika Kumaratunga's ruling People's Alliance (PA) government.
Polling began at 7.00 a.m. (0100 GMT) and officials said voting in the capital Colombo was brisk in the morning.
Some 10 million Sri Lankans are eligible to vote in Friday's polls to elect 3,567 representatives to local bodies.

Election Commissioner Dayananda Dissnayake said on election eve that more than 100,000 public servants were manning 8,246 polling stations across the island, except in the northern and eastern provinces where government troops are fighting Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam Tamil (LTTE) rebels.
No polls are being held in the north and the east due to the unrest.
Nearly 20,000 candidates from 12 political parties and 132 independent groups are in fray for 12 municipal councils, 31 urban councils and 195 smaller local bodies.
The ruling PA is contesting 231 local bodies while the main opposition United National Party (UNP) all 238.
The UNP has said it was concerned that the five week-long election campaign often marred by violence could keep voters away.
"We would like to see over a 60 percent voter turnout. A high poll would work in favour of us," UNP leader and former prime minister Ranil Wickremesinghe said.
The UNP lost power to PA in the 1994 general elections after ruling Sri Lanka for 17 years.
Kumaratunga played down violence and appealed to all political parties to help ensure Friday's elections were peaceful.

"Whatever political party you might belong to, it is the sacred mission of us all to ensure peace and the rule of law and to create for ourselves and our children a civilised society," she said in an eve-of-election statement.
